\section[stressato]{stressato — stressed}

\label{lesson:IT-C362-stressato}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for the training, then the Italian for the consultant.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: stressato}
\textbf{stressato} — \textquotedblleft{}stressed\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
In questo periodo sono molto stressata.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{I am very stressed at the moment.}
\end{quote}

A woman says \emph{stressata}. The noun is \emph{lo stress}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{stressato} is built on \emph{stress}, which was borrowed from English \emph{stress} \textquotedblleft{}strain, pressure\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{stressato}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{stressato}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{stressato}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Italian for the training, then the Italian for the consultant, then say \emph{stressato} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does stressato mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Stressed\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[esaurito]{esaurito — worn out, burnt out; sold out}

\label{lesson:IT-C362-esaurito}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for the consultant, then the Italian for stressed.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: esaurito}
\textbf{esaurito} — \textquotedblleft{}worn out, burnt out; sold out\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Dopo sei mesi senza ferie sono esaurito.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{After six months without holidays I am burnt out.}
\end{quote}

Of tickets or goods: \emph{i biglietti sono esauriti} — sold out.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{esaurito} is the past participle of \emph{esaurire} \textquotedblleft{}to use up\textquotedblright{}, a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{exhaurīre} \textquotedblleft{}to draw out, to drain\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short), built on \emph{haurīre} \textquotedblleft{}to draw water\textquotedblright{}: drained dry.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{esaurito}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{esaurito}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{esaurito}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Italian for the consultant, then the Italian for stressed, then say \emph{esaurito} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does esaurito mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Worn out, burnt out; sold out\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[l'efficienza]{l'efficienza — the efficiency}

\label{lesson:IT-C362-efficienza}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for stressed, then the Italian for worn out.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: l'efficienza}
\textbf{l'efficienza} — \textquotedblleft{}the efficiency\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Con il nuovo computer l'efficienza è aumentata.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{With the new computer, efficiency has gone up.}
\end{quote}

\emph{In piena efficienza} — in full working order.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{efficienza} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{efficientia} \textquotedblleft{}efficiency\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB), from \emph{efficere} \textquotedblleft{}to bring about\textquotedblright{}, built on \emph{facere} \textquotedblleft{}to do\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{l'efficienza}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{l'efficienza}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{l'efficienza}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Italian for stressed, then the Italian for worn out, then say \emph{l'efficienza} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does l'efficienza mean? (\textquotedblleft{}The efficiency\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[efficiente]{efficiente — efficient}

\label{lesson:IT-C362-efficiente}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for worn out, then the Italian for the efficiency.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: efficiente}
\textbf{efficiente} — \textquotedblleft{}efficient\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
La nuova segretaria è molto efficiente.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The new secretary is very efficient.}
\end{quote}

One form for both genders.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{efficiente} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{efficiēns} (EtymDB), present participle of \emph{efficere} \textquotedblleft{}to bring about\textquotedblright{}, built from \emph{ex} and \emph{facere} \textquotedblleft{}to do\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{efficiente}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Italian for worn out, then the Italian for the efficiency, then say \emph{efficiente} again

\section[la produttività]{la produttività — the productivity}

\label{lesson:IT-C362-produttivita}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for the efficiency, then the Italian for efficient.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: la produttività}
\textbf{la produttività} — \textquotedblleft{}the productivity\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Dormire poco abbassa la produttività.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Sleeping too little lowers productivity.}
\end{quote}

The adjective is \emph{produttivo}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{produttività} is built on \emph{produttivo}, a learned borrowing from Late Latin \emph{prōductīvus}, from \emph{prōdūcere} \textquotedblleft{}to bring forth\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short), built on \emph{dūcere} \textquotedblleft{}to lead\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{la produttività}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{la produttività}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{la produttività}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Italian for the efficiency, then the Italian for efficient, then say \emph{la produttività} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does la produttività mean? (\textquotedblleft{}The productivity\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[(dialogue)]{Ripasso dei capitoli 355–362}

\label{lesson:IT-R362-ripasso-355-362}



\begin{quote}
Say the Italian for the remedy and to sort out.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item the remedy, to sort out, to make worse, to soften, to make up for
  \item the CV, the application, to apply, the candidate, the hiring
  \item the dismissal, to resign, the resignation, unemployed, the notice
  \item the internship, the intern, the apprentice, the employer, the employee
  \item the trade union, the strike, to go on strike, the shift, the overtime
  \item the manager, the department, the duty, the extension, the delivery
  \item the rise, the qualification, the skill, the training, the consultant
  \item stressed, worn out, the efficiency, efficient, the productivity
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
The remedy? (\textbf{il rimedio}.) To sort out? (\textbf{sistemare}.) To make worse? (\textbf{aggravare}.) To soften? (\textbf{attenuare}.) To make up for? (\textbf{compensare}.) The CV? (\textbf{il curriculum}.) The application? (\textbf{la candidatura}.) To apply? (\textbf{candidarsi}.) The candidate? (\textbf{il candidato}.) The hiring? (\textbf{l'assunzione}.) The dismissal? (\textbf{il licenziamento}.) To resign? (\textbf{dimettersi}.) The resignation? (\textbf{le dimissioni}.) Unemployed? (\textbf{disoccupato}.) The notice? (\textbf{il preavviso}.) The internship? (\textbf{il tirocinio}.) The intern? (\textbf{il tirocinante}.) The apprentice? (\textbf{l'apprendista}.) The employer? (\textbf{il datore di lavoro}.) The employee? (\textbf{il dipendente}.) The trade union? (\textbf{il sindacato}.) The strike? (\textbf{lo sciopero}.) To go on strike? (\textbf{scioperare}.) The shift? (\textbf{il turno}.) The overtime? (\textbf{gli straordinari}.) The manager? (\textbf{il dirigente}.) The department? (\textbf{il reparto}.) The duty? (\textbf{la mansione}.) The extension? (\textbf{la proroga}.) The delivery? (\textbf{la consegna}.) The rise? (\textbf{l'aumento}.) The qualification? (\textbf{la qualifica}.) The skill? (\textbf{la competenza}.) The training? (\textbf{la formazione}.) The consultant? (\textbf{il consulente}.) Stressed? (\textbf{stressato}.) Worn out? (\textbf{esaurito}.) The efficiency? (\textbf{l'efficienza}.) Efficient? (\textbf{efficiente}.) The productivity? (\textbf{la produttività}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
